Ah, makes sense. However, the problem is that `Object.keys` is not guaranteed to return the keys in any particular order, is it? It seems that there's no good way to get the right order if we're using Redux this way and a run has entries with the same timestamp. We're considering recording a "step" that's an increasing integer for each version of the metric reported to handle this as well as to let users control the X axis coordinates. CC @mparkhe who's thinking about this.
BTW maybe there's also a way to make Redux just keep the original array returned in the JSON instead of expanding these by key.

I agree with @mateiz that `Object.keys` should not guarantee the order of the keys. That being said, the code as is is way overengineered and was designed to merge stuff by timestamp instead of by index. We could implement it in a much cleaner way by simply merging all the lists returned by the calls to `getMetricsByKey(runUuid, metricKey, state)` for each `runUuid`

Hi @cryptexis,

This is a good observation. As @mateiz mentioned, we are looking at augmenting the `Metrics` data model with a notion of an alternative (custom) X-axis measure (in addition to timestamp). This will enable users to optionally log metrics with an alternative X-axis measure, which when present will override the timestamp based X-axis. 

If you have any thoughts on that, will be happy to get more input on that. 

Thanks,
mani

issue.body: ### Related Issues/PRs N/A ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? The `actions/stale` action relies on `updated_at` timestamps, which get bumped by GitHub's internal mergeability checks, preventing abandoned PRs from ever being marked stale. The stale PR workflow was skipping PRs that reference closing keywords (e.g., "Fixes #123"), exempting them from the 30-day inactivity check. This removes that exemption so all member/Copilot PRs are treated uniformly. ### Changes - **`.github/workflows/stale-prs.js`**: Remove `closingIssuesReferences(first: 1) { totalCount }` from the GraphQL query and drop the corresponding early-return guard in `shouldProcessPR` ### Related Issues/PRs ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? Remove the closing-issue exemption from the stale PR workflow. Previously, any PR containing a closing keyword was skipped entirely; now all member/Copilot-authored PRs are subject to the 30-day inactivity check regardless of issue linkage. ### How is this PR tested? - [ ] Manual tests ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] No. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/build`: Build and test infrastructure for MLflow #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/none` - No description will be included. The PR will be mentioned only by the PR number in the "Small Bugfixes and Documentation Updates" section #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release? - [ ] This PR is critical and needs to be in the next patch release - [x] This PR can wait for the next minor release

This exemption should be removed so that all member/Copilot PRs are subject to the 30-day inactivity check, regardless of whether they reference an issue. > > ## Implementation Guide > > ### Relevant Files > > - `.github/workflows/stale-prs.js:26-28` — `closingIssuesReferences` GraphQL field to remove > - `.github/workflows/stale-prs.js:92-95` — `shouldProcessPR` check to remove > > ### Steps > > 1.
